fixes.explanation: Salted and stored, friend? That's a good move for a pantry, but not for this offering. God says what remains on the third day “…must be burned up.” (Leviticus 19:6) I've left plenty of things in the back of a drawer for years, but this offering doesn't get that treatment. Day three, it goes in the fire.

Good guess, friend, since priests and Levites are all over the offerings. But this is the harvest, and God points somewhere else. He says to leave the fallen grapes “…for the poor and the foreigner.” (Leviticus 19:10) So those grapes stay on the ground for them. Think of it as a batch of cookies where you leave a few on the cooling rack on purpose.

Careful, friend, this one is true. Leviticus 19:16 says, “You must not go about spreading slander among your people.” That's a direct command from God, right there in the text. Right next to it comes “You must not endanger the life of your neighbor.” So the passage takes words about a neighbor seriously.

A fine to the priest? Nice try, friend, but nobody is sending a bill in this verse. God says, “You must not turn to mediums or spiritists; do not seek them out, or you will be defiled by them.” (Leviticus 19:31) The result He names is being defiled. I'd take that over any invoice.
